title: A morphism of geometric points induces a bijection of etale stalks
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}k\to S$ and $\bar s':\operatorname{Spec}k'\to S$ be geometric points of $S$ [def-weil-geometric-point] ($k,k'$ algebraically closed fields). Let $a:\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}k'$ be a morphism of schemes with $\bar s'\circ a=\bar s$ (a *morphism of geometric points* $a:\bar s\to\bar s'$). For a pointed etale neighbourhood $(U,\bar u')$ of $\bar s'$ (an object $U\to S$ of the small etale site $S_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] with a lift $\bar u':\operatorname{Spec}k'\to U$ of $\bar s'$), $(U,\bar u'\circ a)$ is a pointed etale neighbourhood of $\bar s$. Then for every sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$ on $S_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] there is exactly one map $a^*:\mathcal F_{\bar s'}\to\mathcal F_{\bar s}$ between the stalks [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] sending the class of $\sigma\in\mathcal F(U)$ at $(U,\bar u')$ to the class of $\sigma$ at $(U,\bar u'\circ a)$, and $a^*$ is bijective; for a sheaf of abelian groups $\mathcal F$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] it is an isomorphism of abelian groups. (The functor $(U,\bar u')\mapsto(U,\bar u'\circ a)$ between the categories of pointed etale neighbourhoods is an equivalence.)

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Remark 04FN (remark-map-stalks, line 3416): the canonical map of stalks of a morphism of geometric points, 'since the functor above is clearly an equivalence ... this canonical map is an isomorphism of stalk functors'; used in the paragraph before Definition 04FS (line 3984)

proof.text: (Morphisms from the spectrum of a field.) For a field $K$ and a scheme $X$, by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field] a morphism $g:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ is the same as a pair $(x,\varphi)$ of a point $x\in X$ and a field homomorphism $\varphi:\kappa(x)\to K$, via $g=j_x\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)$, where $j_x:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$ is the canonical morphism; write $g=(x,\varphi)$. Two rules follow. (i) If $h:X\to Y$ is a morphism and $r_x:\kappa(h(x))\to\kappa(x)$ the induced map of residue fields, then $h\circ(x,\varphi)=(h(x),\varphi\circ r_x)$: by [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality] $h\circ j_x=j_{h(x)}\circ\operatorname{Spec}(r_x)$, so $h\circ g=j_{h(x)}\circ\operatorname{Spec}(r_x)\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)=j_{h(x)}\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi\circ r_x)$ ($\operatorname{Spec}$ is a contravariant functor [def-weil-affine-spectrum]), and the pair is read off by the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field]. (ii) The scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k'$ has a single point $\xi'$, whose residue field is $k'$ itself with $j_{\xi'}=\mathrm{id}$ ([lem-weil-pbc-spec-field-point-residue-field] (1) for the field $R=k'$ and its prime $(0)$); hence by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field] the morphism $a$ is $a=\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha)$ for a unique field homomorphism $\alpha:k'\to k$, which is injective (a ring map between fields). For every $g=(x,\varphi):\operatorname{Spec}k'\to X$ we get $g\circ a=j_x\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha)=j_x\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha\circ\varphi)$, i.e. $g\circ a=(x,\alpha\circ\varphi)$. Consequently precomposition with $a$ is injective on morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}k'\to X$: if $(x_1,\alpha\circ\varphi_1)=(x_2,\alpha\circ\varphi_2)$ then $x_1=x_2$ and $\varphi_1=\varphi_2$ because $\alpha$ is injective.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Remark 04FN (remark-map-stalks, lines 3416-3441): 'the functor above is clearly an equivalence'; written out here

proof.text: (Lifts as field embeddings.) Write $\bar s'=(s,\beta')$ with $s\in S$ and $\beta':\kappa(s)\to k'$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. By step 1 (ii), $\bar s=\bar s'\circ a=(s,\alpha\circ\beta')$, so $\bar s$ lies over the same point $s$. Let $f:U\to S$ be an object of $S_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. By step 1 (i), a morphism $\bar u'=(u,\varphi'):\operatorname{Spec}k'\to U$ satisfies $f\circ\bar u'=\bar s'$ iff $f(u)=s$ and $\varphi'\circ r_u=\beta'$, where $r_u:\kappa(s)\to\kappa(u)$ is induced by $f$; likewise $\bar u=(u,\varphi):\operatorname{Spec}k\to U$ is a lift of $\bar s$ iff $f(u)=s$ and $\varphi\circ r_u=\alpha\circ\beta'$. So the pointed etale neighbourhoods of $\bar s'$ (resp. $\bar s$) [def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods] with underlying $U$ are the triples $(U,u,\varphi')$ (resp. $(U,u,\varphi)$) as above, and the rule $\Phi:(U,\bar u')\mapsto(U,\bar u'\circ a)$ of the statement is $(U,u,\varphi')\mapsto(U,u,\alpha\circ\varphi')$ (step 1 (ii)); in particular $(U,\bar u'\circ a)$ is a pointed etale neighbourhood of $\bar s$, as the statement says.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Remark 04FN (remark-map-stalks, lines 3416-3441): 'the functor above is clearly an equivalence'; written out here

proof.text: ($\Phi$ is bijective on objects.) Fix $U$. Injectivity: $\alpha\circ\varphi'_1=\alpha\circ\varphi'_2$ implies $\varphi'_1=\varphi'_2$ since $\alpha$ is injective. Surjectivity: let $(U,u,\varphi)$ be a pointed etale neighbourhood of $\bar s$, so $f(u)=s$ and $\varphi\circ r_u=\alpha\circ\beta'$. Since $f$ is etale, $\kappa(u)$ is separable algebraic over $\kappa(s)$ through $r_u$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-residue-field-extension-separable], [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Let $y\in\kappa(u)$ and let $P=\sum c_iT^i\in\kappa(s)[T]$ be nonzero with $\sum r_u(c_i)y^i=0$. Applying $\varphi$ gives $\sum\alpha(\beta'(c_i))\varphi(y)^i=0$, and the polynomial $\sum\alpha(\beta'(c_i))T^i$ has coefficients in $\alpha(k')$ and is nonzero ($\alpha\circ\beta'$ is injective). So $\varphi(y)$ is algebraic over $\alpha(k')$, and since $k'$ is algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure], $\varphi(y)\in\alpha(k')$ by [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-over-algebraically-closed-subfield]. Hence $\varphi(\kappa(u))\subseteq\alpha(k')$; as $\alpha:k'\to\alpha(k')$ is a bijective ring map, $\varphi':=\alpha^{-1}\circ\varphi:\kappa(u)\to k'$ is a field homomorphism with $\alpha\circ\varphi'=\varphi$, and $\alpha\circ(\varphi'\circ r_u)=\varphi\circ r_u=\alpha\circ\beta'$ gives $\varphi'\circ r_u=\beta'$ by injectivity of $\alpha$. So $(U,u,\varphi')$ is a pointed etale neighbourhood of $\bar s'$ with $\Phi(U,u,\varphi')=(U,u,\varphi)$.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Remark 04FN (remark-map-stalks, lines 3416-3441): 'the functor above is clearly an equivalence'; written out here

proof.text: ($\Phi$ is an isomorphism of categories.) A morphism $(U,\bar u')\to(V,\bar v')$ of pointed etale neighbourhoods of $\bar s'$ is an $S$-morphism $h:U\to V$ with $h\circ\bar u'=\bar v'$; a morphism $(U,\bar u'\circ a)\to(V,\bar v'\circ a)$ of pointed etale neighbourhoods of $\bar s$ is an $S$-morphism $h$ with $h\circ\bar u'\circ a=\bar v'\circ a$ [def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods]. By the injectivity of precomposition with $a$ (step 1 (ii), applied to $X=V$) the two conditions on $h$ are equivalent. Hence $\Phi$, defined on morphisms by $h\mapsto h$, is a functor that is bijective on every set of morphisms and (step 3) on objects: an isomorphism of categories $\mathcal N_{\bar s'}\to\mathcal N_{\bar s}$, compatible with the functors to $S_{\Et}$ forgetting the lift. (This is the equivalence asserted in Stacks 04FN, in the stronger form of an isomorphism.)

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Remark 04FN (remark-map-stalks, lines 3416-3441): 'the functor above is clearly an equivalence'; written out here

proof.text: (The map of stalks.) By [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], $\mathcal F_{\bar s'}=\varinjlim_{\mathcal N_{\bar s'}^{\mathrm{op}}}D'$ and $\mathcal F_{\bar s}=\varinjlim_{\mathcal N_{\bar s}^{\mathrm{op}}}D$ with $D'(U,\bar u')=\mathcal F(U)$, $D(U,\bar u)=\mathcal F(U)$ and both sending a morphism $h$ to $\mathcal F(h)$; by step 4, $D'=D\circ\Phi^{\mathrm{op}}$. The universal property of $\varinjlim D'$ gives the map $a^*$ with $a^*([U,\bar u',\sigma])=[U,\bar u'\circ a,\sigma]$ (the coprojections $\mathcal F(U)=D(\Phi(U,\bar u'))\to\mathcal F_{\bar s}$ form a cocone on $D'$; Stacks Categories, Lemma 002K, categories-lemma-functorial-colimit, with $t=\mathrm{id}$), and it is the only map with this property because every element of a colimit of sets is the class of some $\sigma\in D'(U,\bar u')$. In the same way $\Phi^{-1}$ gives $b:\mathcal F_{\bar s}\to\mathcal F_{\bar s'}$ with $b([U,\bar u'\circ a,\sigma])=[U,\bar u',\sigma]$; as every element of $\mathcal F_{\bar s}$ has the form $[\Phi(U,\bar u'),\sigma]$ (step 3), $b\circ a^*$ and $a^*\circ b$ are the identity on all classes, so $a^*$ is bijective. If $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf of abelian groups [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], its stalks are the colimits of the same diagrams in abelian groups; the index categories are cofiltered [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered], so these filtered colimits have the colimits of the underlying sets as underlying sets, and $a^*$, being induced by the additive coprojections, is additive; a bijective additive map is an isomorphism of abelian groups.

split_report.summary: Read Stacks Remark 04FN (etale-cohomology.tex 3416-3441; it only asserts the functor is 'clearly an equivalence'). Wrote the proof by agent in five steps: morphisms Spec K -> X as pairs (point, field map) with the composition rules (lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field, lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality, lem-weil-pbc-spec-field-point-residue-field), a = Spec(alpha) and precomposition with a injective; lifts of s-bar' / s-bar to U as kappa(s)-embeddings of kappa(u); bijectivity on objects from the separability (algebraicity) of kappa(u)/kappa(s) for etale U -> S (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-etale-residue-field-extension-separable) and the fact that an element algebraic over the algebraically closed alpha(k') lies in alpha(k') (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-over-algebraically-closed-subfield); the functor is an isomorphism of categories (not just an equivalence); the stalk map is the comparison map of colimits along it, bijective, additive for abelian sheaves. Statement and stmt_deps kept; the clause about modules does not occur in Stacks 04FN (it speaks of 'stalk functors' only), the item's abelian clause is covered. lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points and lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift were not needed.
